title: Injectable Supramolecular Polymer-Nanoparticle Hydrogels for Cell and Drug Delivery Applications
protocol: Synthesize HPMC-C12 and PEG-PLA using previously published methods.
Measure 50 mg of PEG-PLA polymer into an 8 mL glass scintillation vial.
Add 1 mL of acetonitrile to the vial containing PEG-PLA polymer.
Vortex the solution to fully dissolve the polymer.
Add 10 mL of ultrapure water into a 20 mL glass scintillation vial with a small stir bar.
Set the stir plate to 600 rpm and begin stirring the water in the vial.
Add 1 mL of dissolved PEG-PLA polymer solution dropwise into the stirred ultrapure water using a 200 µL pipette.
Stir for 2 minutes after adding the polymer solution.
Verify the particle size by dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Dilute 20 µL of NP solution with 80 µL of ultrapure water (analysis concentration: 1 mg/mL PEG-PLA NPs).
Add 30 µL per well to a clear bottom black 384-well plate (analyze in triplicate).
Measure the hydrodynamic radius and polydispersity of each sample with a DLS plate reader using preset protocol options in the software package.
Set data collection parameters to acquire 5-10 DLS measurements of 2-5 s duration per acquisition.
Report a mean particle size and distribution per well, calculated from the globular proteins model.
Resuspend NPs in PBS to achieve a 20 wt% NP solution.
Pipette the contents of the centrifugal filter unit into a tared microcentrifuge tube or glass scintillation vial on a mass balance.
Rinse the filter with 50-100 µL of buffer to ensure all NPs are collected.
Add buffer to reach a total mass of 250 mg.
Prepare a stock solution of 6 wt% HPMC-C12 in PBS and dissolve for 48 hours.
Transfer 333 mg of the 6 wt% HPMC-C12 stock solution into a 1 mL Luer lock syringe.
Add 500 µL of 20 wt% NP stock solution to a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 167 µL of PBS and pipette to mix.
Fill a 1 mL Luer lock syringe with the diluted NP solution using a needle.
Mix 500 µL of HPMC-C12 solution with the NP solution in the syringe.
Attach a Luer elbow connector to the syringe containing NP solution.
Push the NP solution through the elbow until the meniscus is visible at the open end.
Connect the syringe containing HPMC-C12 solution to the other side of the elbow connector.
Pump the two solutions back and forth through the elbow mixer for approximately 60 cycles until a homogeneous, opaque white hydrogel material has formed.
Push the entire volume of hydrogel into one syringe.
Remove the empty syringe and draw the plunger back on the gel-loaded syringe to recover material from the elbow connector.
Cap with a needle or plug.
Account for ~300 µL of lost hydrogel volume due to dead space in the mixing process.
Formulate at least 700 µL of PNP hydrogel for rheological characterization.
Store the hydrogel in the syringe at room temperature.
If drugs are encapsulated, store the material at 4 °C unless specified otherwise by the drug manufacturer.
Do not freeze the material.
Inject material in the center of the serrated rheometer plate.
Lower the rheometer to the trim gap (500-1000 µm).
Slowly turn the top rheometer plate as it makes contact with the PNP hydrogel.
Inspect the loading of the PNP hydrogel to ensure it covers the entire rheometer plate surface.
Use a spatula or plastic trimmer to gently trim and remove any excess material.
Lower the rheometer to the final geometry gap.
Verify that the sample is cleanly loaded.
Measure the mechanical properties of the sample using oscillatory tests, such as amplitude or frequency sweeps, or flow tests, such as flow sweeps or step tests.
Cut glass capillary tubes to desired length for in vitro drug release testing.
Seal one end of each tube by pushing a small amount of epoxy into the end of the tube with a disposable spatula or pipette tip.
Formulate at least 500 µl of PNP hydrogel material in a syringe containing the drug of interest.
Prepare each sample group in a separate syringe.
Inject 100-200 μl of PNP hydrogel at the bottom of each capillary tube using a long hypodermic needle (22G, 4 inch).
Centrifuge filled capillary tubes for 1 min at 1000 x g to ensure uniform surface of the hydrogel.
Fill 200-300 μl of PBS on top of the hydrogel in the capillary tube using a syringe and needle or pipette without disturbing the surface of the hydrogel.
Seal the capillary tubes with a cap, plug, or paraffin film.
Incubate samples at 37°C to simulate in vivo conditions.
Carefully remove PBS from each capillary without disturbing the hydrogel surface using a syringe and needle.
Replace removed volume with fresh PBS.
Store aliquots under appropriate conditions.
Formulate at least 1.2 mL of PNP hydrogel per sample group.
Load both insulin (drug cargo) and thioflavin T (ThT) (molecular probe) into the PNP hydrogel following the procedure described in section 2.3.
Inject 200 µL of PNP hydrogel per well into a black 96-well plate.
Seal the plate with an optically clear adhesive plate seal to prevent evaporation.
Insert the plate into a plate reader equipped with temperature control, shaking, and kinetic read programming.
Begin the read protocol using excitation/emission at 450 nm/482 nm at 20 min intervals.
Formulate at least 2 mL of PNP hydrogel containing the desired cell concentration.
Prepare each sample group in a separate syringe.
Inject 150 µL PNP hydrogel into each well in a clear bottom 96-well plate.
Centrifuge the plate at 50 x g for 2 min to spread the hydrogel evenly in the well.
Add 100 µL of the appropriate cell media on top of the hydrogel.
Remove this media each day and add 100 µL new media.
On Day 1, remove the media on top of the hydrogel for the designated replicates for that time point for each sample group.
Add 50 µL of 2 mM calcein AM solution on top of the hydrogels.
Incubate for 30 min.
Image the center of each well in a 96-well plate using a confocal microscope.
Survey an area of at least 300 µm² with a z-stack spanning at least 150 µm.
Capture the fluorescence of calcein (excitation/emission: 495 nm/515 nm).
Collapse all z-stack images into a single plane maximum intensity image using FIJI or similar software.
Quantify the number of fluorescent cells in each image.
Calculate the ratio of the number of fluorescent cells at each time point compared to the number of fluorescent cells at Day 1 as the relative cell viability in the PNP hydrogels.
Assess cell settling by calculating the number of cells required to formulate 500-700 µL of PNP hydrogel at a final concentration of 5 x 10⁶ cells/mL.
Suspend cells in 1 mL of PBS at a concentration of 1 x 10⁶ cells/mL.
Stain cells by adding 50 µL of 2 mM calcein AM.
Incubate the cells with the dye for 10 min.
Centrifuge cells at appropriate conditions.
Remove PBS from centrifuged cells.
Resuspend cells in PBS to form 500-700 µL of PNP hydrogel.
Inject 100-200 µL of PNP hydrogel containing stained cells into the bottom of a cuvette using a 21G needle.
Move the needle back and forth while injecting to prevent bubble formation.
Image cuvettes lying on their side immediately after injection over the entire flat area at the base of the cuvette.
Use confocal tile scanning capabilities to image the entire well area in 3D across a 100 µm depth.
Perform maximum intensity projection using confocal microscope software or FIJI software for later visualization.
Stand cuvettes upright following imaging.
Image cuvettes again at 1 h and 4 h to observe cell settlement or suspension.
Collapse all z-stack images into a single plane maximum intensity image.
Quantify the cell distribution using FIJI or similar software.
Measure the fluorescence intensity down the center vertical profile of the cuvette.
